source.title: Feature Dynamics as Implicit Data Augmentation: A Depth-Decomposed View on Deep Neural Network Generalization
source.authors: Tian-Yu Ruan; Kuo Gai; Shi-Hua Zhang

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendices, is present; some equations and figure content are flattened, but no relevant section appears cut off.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests whether a different measured property—prediction consistency across composites of network checkpoints—relates to generalization, including under test, corrupted, and noisy-label conditions. It does not test the specific interventions or measures in V1–V8.
record.gate_note: The study reports temporal-consistency results and test-performance changes after reinitializing deeper layers or freezing shallow layers. These bear on generalization but do not measure the behavior named by V1–V8. Figure-only curves and distributions without textual numeric results are not extracted as numeric rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures temporal prediction consistency, SGD-induced feature noise, and the effects of freezing or reinitializing layers. None tests V1–V8. In particular, consistency under 40% randomized labels does not measure random-label fitting or held-out accuracy as required by V1.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors interpret temporal consistency as implicit structured augmentation that supports generalization and robustness, report its weakening under randomized labels, and identify anisotropic SGD-induced feature noise. Their proposed bridge to generalization remains conceptual, with practical estimators left to future work.
record.recipe_differences: Measures temporal consistency across composites of network checkpoints and relates it conceptually to generalization; does not use the original versions’ memorization, architecture, optimizer, batch-size, regularization, sharpness, or example-removal comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: Consistency changes with label condition: clean-label results are concentrated near 1.0, while results with 40% randomized labels collapse. Test performance after reinitializing deeper layers also varies with how many initial blocks are retained.

fits_no_version.finding: Checkpoint composites show high prediction consistency on clean and corrupted test inputs after clean-label training; consistency weakens with 40% randomized training labels.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Temporal prediction consistency depends on meaningful training supervision and can persist on unseen and corrupted inputs.

fits_no_version.finding: Freezing retained shallow layers and retraining reinitialized deeper layers modestly worsens clean accuracy and corruption error; freezing shallow layers during continued training also slightly worsens accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: These layer interventions reduce performance relative to fully trained or fully trainable baselines in the tested ResNet-20 setting.

record.problems: The main consistency distributions and several performance curves are presented in figures without numeric values in the text. The reported clean test-accuracy changes after reinitialization are modest, and the freezing comparison gives no exact values. The paper does not directly measure the train–test error gap for the claim versions.
record.rows_left_out: No additional textually stated results matching the extracted measures were omitted. Other consistency curves and corruption-type distributions in Figures 2–8 and 10–18 are figure-only or provide no separate textual numeric values; exact values were not inferred from plots.

untested.parts: Coexistence of near-perfect random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same recipe, and chance held-out accuracy with random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under controlled tuning, including recovery strategies.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and changes from adapting the training recipe.
Dropout effects, dependence on training-set size or dropout strength, and joint removal with weight decay under augmentation.
Magnitude-aware weight sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and its ranking relative to other measures.
Accuracy after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: States are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because all rows measure other constructs or interventions. This does not dispute the reported findings. Different optimizers across different datasets in Table 2 do not constitute a controlled V4 comparison.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test fitting random labels to near zero training error, compare natural-label test accuracy with chance, or report random-label held-out accuracy.
No width sweep or test-error comparison around or beyond the interpolation threshold.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks or of their connectivity.
No controlled comparison of adaptive optimizers and SGD generalization.
No batch-size comparison of generalization under fixed epoch budgets.
No dropout intervention or comparison of dropout and weight decay.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare it with generalization gaps or other measures.
Does not identify or remove memorized examples and measure the resulting test-accuracy change.

rows.subject: ResNet-20
rows.stage_stated: trained on CIFAR-10 with clean labels; epochs 200–300
rows.operation_detail: Measured consistency of composite and reference predictions on the CIFAR-10 test set.
rows.measure: Prediction consistency distribution; described as sharply concentrated near 1.0.
rows.note: Measures composite-model consistency, not test error or accuracy.
rows.check: Prediction agreement across checkpoint composites cannot establish any claim version; high agreement need not mean correct predictions.

rows.subject: ResNet-20
rows.stage_stated: trained on CIFAR-10 with clean labels; epochs 200–300
rows.operation_detail: Measured consistency on CIFAR-10C with Gaussian blur at severity 5.
rows.measure: Prediction consistency distribution; described as sharply concentrated near 1.0.
rows.note: The paper also describes consistency near 1.0 across corruption types in Appendix Figure 16; no individual numeric values are stated.
rows.check: Consistency on corrupted inputs measures a different construct from V1–V8.

rows.subject: ResNet-20
rows.stage_stated: trained on CIFAR-10 with 40% randomized training labels; epochs 200–300
rows.operation_detail: Measured consistency on CIFAR-10 under randomized training labels.
rows.measure: Consistency distribution; described as collapsed, with long tails and mass shifted away from 1.0.
rows.baseline: Clean-label training: distribution sharply concentrated near 1.0
rows.value: collapsed; long tails emerge and mass shifts away from 1.0
rows.note: Consistency is not held-out accuracy or random-label fit.
rows.check: Lower consistency is not a reversal of V1. Table 1 assigns the reported p-value to Depth 1, without identifying it as a CIFAR-10-specific comparison.

rows.subject: ResNet-20
rows.stage_stated: trained on CIFAR-10 with 40% randomized training labels; epochs 200–300
rows.operation_detail: Measured consistency on CIFAR-10C under randomized training labels.
rows.measure: Consistency distribution; described as collapsed, with long tails and mass shifted away from 1.0.
rows.baseline: Clean-label training: distribution sharply concentrated near 1.0
rows.value: collapsed; long tails emerge and mass shifts away from 1.0
rows.note: Consistency is not held-out accuracy or random-label fit.
rows.check: Lower consistency is not a reversal of any version. Table 1 assigns the reported p-value to Depth 2, without identifying it as a CIFAR-10C-specific comparison.

rows.subject: ResNet-20
rows.stage_stated: trained on CIFAR-10; deeper layers reinitialized and retrained
rows.operation_detail: Retained the first basic block and reinitialized deeper layers before retraining.
rows.note: The authors describe the degradation as modest.
rows.check: The accuracy values match the text, but the condition must specify that retained shallow layers were frozen while reinitialized deeper layers were retrained. This intervention tests none of V1–V8.

rows.subject: ResNet-20
rows.stage_stated: trained on CIFAR-10; deeper layers reinitialized and retrained
rows.operation_detail: Retained the first two basic blocks and reinitialized deeper layers before retraining.
rows.note: The authors state that preserving shallow representations alone is insufficient to fully recover the original performance.
rows.check: The accuracy values match the text, but retained shallow layers were frozen while reinitialized deeper layers were retrained. This is not a partial effect for any claim version.

rows.subject: ResNet-20
rows.stage_stated: trained on CIFAR-10; deeper layers reinitialized and retrained
rows.operation_detail: Retained the first basic block and reinitialized deeper layers before retraining.

conditions.value: mean corruption error across 15 corruption types and 5 severities

rows.note: The paper defines mCE as the unnormalized average error.
rows.check: Specify frozen retained shallow layers and retraining of reinitialized deeper layers. The mCE change measures none of V1–V8.

rows.subject: ResNet-20
rows.stage_stated: trained on CIFAR-10; deeper layers reinitialized and retrained
rows.operation_detail: Retained the first two basic blocks and reinitialized deeper layers before retraining.

conditions.value: mean corruption error across 15 corruption types and 5 severities

rows.note: The paper describes this as a 3–4% accuracy drop under corruptions.
rows.check: Specify frozen retained shallow layers. The mCE increase from 0.316 to 0.329 equals a 1.3 percentage-point drop in average corruption accuracy; the paper's 3–4% accuracy-drop description is inconsistent with its definition and values.

rows.subject: ResNet-20
rows.stage_stated: trained on CIFAR-10; shallow layers frozen at epoch 150, deeper layers continued training with SGD
rows.operation_detail: Froze the shallow network up to depth d and continued training the deeper layers.
rows.baseline: Fully trainable baseline (SGD); exact value not stated
rows.value: slightly lower and less stable test accuracy
rows.note: No exact accuracy values are given in the text.
rows.check: Freezing layers tests none of V1–V8. The row also pools three distinct conditions, Fix Depth1/2/3; separate them if retaining one row per condition.
